chapter_title: The Pico Kit Hardware and Wiring
learning_objective: The learner will identify which of the five kit parts performs each of 5 described jobs, with at least 4 of 5 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: infographic **sim-id:** kit-parts-infographic
**Library:** html
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Remember
**Bloom Verb:** identify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will identify which of the five kit parts performs each of 5 described jobs, with at least 4 of 5 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** the five parts and their one-line jobs, listed in the table "The Kit Bill of Materials" above this block. **Evidence of Mastery:** The learner is shown 5 job statements one at a time and picks the matching part from the five. A pick is correct when it matches the Correct part column in Content. Mastery is 4 of 5 on the first attempt. Selecting a part to read its description beforehand is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) The Pico itself contains the microphone and speaker. (2) The amplifier makes the sound by itself. (3) The buttons are wired to the display. **Instructional Rationale:** A Remember-level objective asks the learner to recall a fact accurately. Reading a labeled picture first, then answering a job question from memory, gives both a cue to learn from and a retrieval attempt that strengthens recall. **Content:** The infographic shows the five parts as a labeled picture. Selecting a part reveals its name and description. | Part | Description shown on selection | |---|---| | Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W | The brain. It runs your MicroPython program and connects to Wi-Fi. | | Round display | The face. A 360 by 360 color screen that shows text, shapes, and meters. | | INMP441 microphone | The ear. It senses sound and sends 24-bit digital numbers to the Pico. | | MAX98357A amplifier and speaker | The voice. The amplifier turns digital audio into power for the speaker. | | Mode, Up, and Down buttons | The hands. Three switches you press to change modes, settings, and to talk. | Job statements, in this order: | # | Job statement shown to the learner | Correct part | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Turns room sound into digital numbers. | INMP441 microphone | The converter is built into the microphone board. | | 2 | Runs the MicroPython program. | Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W | The Pico is the only part that runs your code. | | 3 | Drives the speaker from digital audio. | MAX98357A amplifier and speaker | The amplifier takes I2S audio and powers the speaker. | | 4 | Shows a level meter and text. | Round display | The display draws what the Pico tells it to draw. | | 5 | Lets the student start push-to-talk. | Mode, Up, and Down buttons | A held button is read as a signal on a Pico pin. | **Provenance:** The parts and jobs come from the chapter section "The Kit Bill of Materials." **Rules:** Each job statement has exactly one correct part. The five parts are always offered together, in a fixed order. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner selects any part to read its description. 2. The learner starts the check. Job statement 1 is shown with the five parts as choices. 3. The learner picks one part. 4. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text, then moves to the next statement. 5. After statement 5, the sim shows the score. **Feedback:** 5 statements, fixed order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: ". Incorrect: "Not quite. This is the job of the : ". The correct part is revealed right after each pick, and a running score "n of 5" is shown. **Starting State:** The five parts are shown labeled and unselected, with the instruction "Select a part to learn its job." **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter names the five parts as the Pico 2 W, the round display, the microphone, the amplifier with a speaker, and the three buttons.
